description:
ExecuteBeadWorker.Run() is a 700-line function with 24 returns: 4 legitimate terminal exits, 1 legacy idle-loop exit, 1 routing-preflight-kills-worker exit, and 18 store-error escalations from the same handleOutcomeStoreError pattern repeated across outcome paths. The implicit state machine in the loop is real and coherent (Pick -> Gate -> Claim -> Execute -> Classify -> Reviewing -> Terminal) but written as conditional soup instead of explicit state.

## Three-package split aligned to FEAT-010

  cli/internal/agent/run/   - Layer 1: invocation atom (existing dispatch + runner)
  cli/internal/agent/try/   - Layer 2: bead attempt (worktree, prompt, single Execute, Land, conflict-recovery, post-merge review, triage)
  cli/internal/agent/work/  - Layer 3: queue drain (pick, claim, heartbeat, drain-loop control, stop conditions)

try.Attempt(beadID) returns sealed Outcome { Disposition (enum), Cooldown, ParkReason, RecordEvents }. Loop becomes approximately 30 lines: pick -> guard -> claim -> attemptWithHeartbeat -> applyOutcome. Single commitOutcome helper deletes the 18 store-error returns.

## Ordering: refactor-LAST per user decision

In-flight Group A beads (c6e3db02 rate-limit, b24e9630 no_changes, cfedee8e ladder wire, a8718bec cost-cap reviewer) land first against current code. dc157075 tactical worker-stay-alive lands first as operational bridge. The stdout/watch-mode beads (ddx-7d9e1e82, ddx-f9acb86d, ddx-7dcbd40b, ddx-8b7ed960, ddx-dc300be9) define the public work-loop contract this refactor must preserve. THIS refactor lands last and absorbs all intervening behavior into the new architecture. Per-child ACs explicitly call out which in-flight bead's behavior each child must preserve.

## Naming and public semantics

Package = try (not try_bead - Go idiom). Function = try.Attempt(beadID). Loop = work.Worker.Drain. CLI surface is ddx run / ddx try / ddx work. ddx work has three modes: once (one ready bead then exit), drain (default: run ready work until no execution-ready beads remain, then exit), and watch (stay alive indefinitely, sleep for idle interval when no execution-ready beads exist, and poll for newly arriving work). The removed polling flag is not preserved as a public compatibility alias; the durable vocabulary is mode plus idle_interval.

## Children

  C0  Pre-refactor JSONL fixture baseline for event-shape regression detection
  C1  try.Outcome sealed sum type + Disposition enum + ParkReason vocabulary enumeration
  C2  try.Attempt function shell (wraps existing executor; no behavior change)
  C3  Move review verdict handling into try.Attempt (180 lines from loop body)
  C4  Move conflict recovery into try.Attempt
  C5  Move no_changes adjudication, decomposition, push-failed, push-conflict (absorbs ddx-b24e9630, ddx-c6e3db02 behavior)
  C6  Single commitOutcome helper; deletes 18 store-error exit paths + handleOutcomeStoreError
  C7  Uniform Guard contract; delete attempted/hookFailed maps; pick() derives from drain.result
  C8  Routing preflight moves to Drain startup (runs once, not per iteration)
  C9  First-class StopCondition enum + cost-cap relocation + downstream-consumer audit for execution_failed:max-cost grep before relocation. Includes queue snapshot plumbing and human-review blocker pressure from ddx-7dcbd40b.
  C10 ddx work once/drain/watch modes + transient idle substate. Watch mode owns idle interval sleeps, per-idle queue status, and next-ready transition messaging from ddx-f9acb86d and ddx-8b7ed960.
  C11 Heartbeat extracted to withHeartbeat helper
  C12 Single phase-event emission (replaces 4 sites)
  C13 File and identifier rename per package split + ADD ddx try CLI command + handle dc157075 file-path migration if it landed first
  C14 Delete ExecuteBead* shims; verify all callers ported off (grep audit)

description:
PROBLEM
Operators cannot evaluate whether reusable attempt workspaces reduce Niflheim-style repeated cold lefthook and Rust build costs because the attempt path emits no time-saved or bytes-saved estimates for reused workspace state.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces without emitting savings values.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` does not expose reusable slot outcome metadata that can carry savings estimate inputs.
- No savings counters exist in the attempt path, leaving no signal for cold starts, time saved, or bytes saved.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, the child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", the child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Add conservative reusable-workspace savings estimates for time saved and bytes saved, derived from the reusable workspace outcome data already available to execute-bead orchestration. Emit those values through the existing execution event/observability path for both reused and cold-start attempts, using zero savings for misses/cold starts where no prior state was reused.

NON-SCOPE

description:
EPIC

Eliminate the .ddx/ footprint from arbitrary git repos using DDx, while keeping today's in-tree behavior available for projects that want it (DDx itself, HELIX, etc.). Make init effectively touchless: zero ceremony for the common case.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE

Single rule: presence of <project>/.ddx/ determines the DDx root.
- If <project>/.ddx/ exists → in-tree mode. Root = <project>/.ddx/. Operator commits or gitignores per their own .gitignore. DDx never manipulates .gitignore.
- If <project>/.ddx/ does NOT exist → convention mode. Root = ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ (defaults to ~/.local/share/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/). The XDG directory is itself a git repo containing all DDx state for that project; the project's own git repo stays pristine.

PROJECT ID is the human-readable remote URL host/owner/repo triple, parsed from `git remote get-url origin`. SSH URLs (`git@github.com:easel/ddx.git`) and HTTPS URLs both resolve to the same path. Projects without a remote fall back to `local/<basename>-<abs-path-short-hash>/`. The slashes are filesystem-real, so the XDG path is browsable: `~/.local/share/ddx/projects/github.com/easel/ddx/`.

OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE at command time:
1. In-tree (<project>/.ddx/config.yaml) — top priority
2. Global (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml) — installed by `ddx init --global`
3. Convention defaults — baked into the binary

Each layer is a delta on the one below. A project with no overrides commits zero new files and writes zero files into its worktree.

ENGINEERING IMPERATIVE

EVERY path in the codebase that today reads or writes under .ddx/ must route through a single DDxRoot(ctx) resolver. No filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...) calls outside that resolver. A regression linter asserts this invariant. The audit is the hard part of this epic.

KNOWN-HARD QUESTION (worth solving but not blocking):

When multiple worktrees of the same project (same remote URL) exist on one machine — e.g. `~/Projects/ddx` and `~/work/ddx-experiment` — they share the same XDG state. SHAs in events are unambiguous, but operator UX for "where do I cd to inspect this" is. Solution direction: each XDG project keeps a worktrees.json registry. One entry is marked master (operator pin or first-seen). Cross-references in audit logs and bead show output cite the master path.

CHILD BEADS

- E1: config: DDxRoot resolver + audit every .ddx/ path writer
- E2: config: convention mode bootstrap (XDG git repo + worktree registry)
- E3: config: ddx init --global installs user-tier skills/personas
- E4: config: ddx init creates .ddx/ in project, switches to in-tree mode
- E5: config: optional .ddx/config.yaml overlay for per-project overrides

NON-SCOPE
- Migration of existing in-tree repos (today's DDx repo, HELIX) is a separate concern. They stay in-tree mode by virtue of having .ddx/ already.
- Server-backed state (federation) is orthogonal. XDG state can be a git repo with a remote; pushing that remote IS the team-share mechanism.
- Manifest-only mode is rejected — the convention/in-tree split makes a separate manifest file unnecessary.

description:
PROBLEM
The candidate-cycle abstraction has deterministic Checks and Repair seams, but production wires only Reviewer. The real repository gate runs after LLM review and a failure immediately preserves the candidate; the existing RepairContext is ignored. DDx therefore neither checks before review nor asks Fizeau to repair a fixable gate failure in the same attempt workspace.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:376-389 constructs applyWorkerCandidateCycle with Reviewer and NoReview while Checks and Repair are nil.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:475-491 and cli/cmd/try.go:452-467 run checks after candidate review.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:390-467 preserves a failed repository gate without a repair operation.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:398-417 creates RepairContext, but execute_bead_loop.go:4207-4236 does not execute it.
- cli/internal/agent/repair_prompt.go:8-70 lacks the full original task, current diff, and deterministic failure output required for an executable repair request.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the production candidate cycle so deterministic repository checks run before review. On a fixable check or review failure, submit a fresh public Fizeau Execute operation in the same DDx attempt worktree using the original task, current diff, and failure evidence. Preserve the primary operation MinPower and immutable operator passthrough exactly; do not set a concrete route. Append the repair commit, rerun checks, then review. Keep the repair budget bounded and durable in attempt evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not invent or call a Continue or resume API, invoke a provider CLI, raise power inside the current attempt, change Fizeau internals, or implement new-attempt escalation policy.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-b8cacbeb. Depends on ddx-8bcf71e0 so repair inherits the route-neutral reviewer and immutable passthrough contract.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification by reading migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and checking field fidelity. That verification should be independently testable from write-path and CLI routing work.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer enables verification through MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If the verifier is absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when Axon data drifts from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so --verify reads back the Axon target, compares migrated source beads field-for-field for the imported corpus, detects drift with an error naming the affected bead ID and field, and passes cleanly after a normal import. For large corpora, keep the implementation compatible with sample-based verification if the existing codebase already has a corpus-size threshold; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

Agents can create contradictory mixed_commit outputs by committing in-scope work and also writing no_changes_rationale.txt, forcing the orchestrator to salvage or park the attempt.

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:4952-4955 then sees repeated mixed_commits at the circuit-breaker layer, where prompt-originated contradictions can trigger OA behavior.

Update the execution prompt guidance so agents are told that if they committed in-scope work, they must not write no_changes_rationale.txt, and that suite-health decisions belong to the orchestrator after the candidate is produced.

NON-SCOPE

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-45ea2e36 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Attempt 20260713T145533-c006900a for ddx-8a78ee90 ran for 32m43s with a populated Codex route, repeatedly executing a known-doomed 600-second package suite. The documented 30-minute running-phase watchdog did not fire because route activity kept the attempt classified as healthy. Operator intervention was required to release the lease and stop CPU/I/O consumption.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3524-3539 installs only the phase-empty progress watchdog for the attempt lifetime.
- cli/internal/agent/work/watchdog.go:49-80 resets the phase-empty timer whenever harness, model, or route is populated, so a routed model can stay active indefinitely while making no useful progress.
- cli/internal/agent/types.go:415-421 gives the provider a separate three-hour absolute wall-clock cap, which is too broad to serve as a queue-attempt lease budget.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:32-39 kills only the original provider process group; ddx-7df6b12a owns the attempt controller required to include descendants that call setsid or reparent.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a work/try active-attempt wall-clock budget with a 30-minute default, an explicit operator override for legitimate longer work, and an explicit zero value to disable only when requested. Run it beside the existing phase-empty watchdog. On expiry, cancel the attempt, release its lease, append operator_attention with bead ID, attempt ID, elapsed time, configured budget, and last activity, and continue draining. Terminate all attempt-controller members through the controller introduced by ddx-7df6b12a so session-changing and reparented tool children cannot survive. Use the same default and override semantics for manual/offline and server-managed workers.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go and cli/internal/agent/work watchdog helpers/tests
- cli/cmd/work.go and cli/cmd/try.go for shared flag/config plumbing
- attempt-controller integration points introduced by ddx-7df6b12a
- operator-attention rendering/tests for the new timeout reason

NON-SCOPE
Do not shorten the generic ddx run three-hour provider cap. Do not change queue ordering, provider routing, the phase-empty watchdog, or long-running bead acceptance commands. Do not rely on process ancestry alone.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root reliability incident. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for attempt-controller members
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... -run "^(TestWorkAttemptWallClock_(PopulatedRouteCannotEvadeDeadline|ReleasesLeaseAndContinuesQueue|ManualManagedParity|ReapsSessionChangingDescendants))$" -count=1 -timeout 120s passes.
- cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... -timeout 600s passes.
- lefthook run pre-commit passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

`cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-100` defines and exports `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, and `NewWatcherHub` from the public `bead` package, while `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:109-224` keeps the polling `projectWatcher` internals in the same public package. The concrete watcher implementation lives in `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-224` instead of `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/`, so the concrete type and constructor are part of the public `bead` package API. The public interface boundary already exists at `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:144-147`, but the implementation is not separated from it.

PROPOSED FIX
Move the concrete watcher implementation from `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go` to `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/watcher_hub.go` with package name `lifecycle`. Keep `LifecycleEvent` in the public `bead` package, update the internal lifecycle implementation to reference `bead.LifecycleEvent`, and keep `LifecycleSubscriber` as the public interface. description:
PROBLEM
DDx-owned temporary homes, provider shims, and helper scratch are created directly under raw os.TempDir(), so /tmp remains the choke point even when DDx has a configured execution/runtime temp root with available space. The 2026-07-08 incident had /tmp at 100% inode use while the configured execution worktree root under /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt still had capacity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:91 creates provider shims with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-provider-shim-").
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29 and runner_test.go:56 create ddx-home-* with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-home-"); equivalent command tests create the same prefix in cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80, cli/cmd/try_test.go:823, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:116 creates ddx-fixture-bin-* with os.MkdirTemp("", ...).
These producers bypass config.ExecutionScratchRoot / config.ExecutionWorktreeRoot and strand inode-heavy scratch under /tmp.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared helper for DDx-owned scratch temp dirs that prefers config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot) or the configured execution/runtime root when a project root is available, and falls back to os.TempDir() only when no configured root exists. Migrate provider shims and DDx-owned temp homes/fixture bins to the helper where production/runtime context is available. Keep tests hermetic by setting the helper root explicitly in tests.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go
- cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go or a new scratch-temp helper package
- relevant tests in cli/internal/agent and cli/cmd

NON-SCOPE
Do not move claim-liveness in this bead; ddx-3986b89a covers claim heartbeat root selection. Do not change git worktree placement. Do not store long-lived user config in execution scratch. Do not require a project root for all tests; fallback behavior must remain.

description:
PROBLEM
When the pre-claim decomposition model returns invalid or empty output, the deterministic fallback can create malformed children that are not independently executable. On 2026-07-13 it split ddx-e6abf4a6 into two partial implementation beads plus a verification-only child, omitted sibling dependencies, duplicated and contradicted the parent context, and failed to place the required package and lefthook gates on every implementation child. An operator had to rewrite and rewire the queue manually.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:480-539 chooses child count from the raw number of numbered AC lines and chunks those lines without distinguishing implementation criteria from shared verification gates or dependency order. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:587-603 embeds a truncated parent description beneath newly generated PROBLEM and ROOT CAUSE headings, preserving stale PARENT/DEPS text and creating contradictory child prompts. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:606-619 adds go test and lefthook only when those strings are absent anywhere in the parent acceptance, so existing gates become their own chunk instead of being copied to each executable child. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:456-477 validates only non-empty title, description, and acceptance and therefore accepts children that fail the repository bead-authoring floor.

PROPOSED FIX
Make deterministic fallback fail safe. Separate implementation ACs from shared build gates, copy required go test and lefthook gates to every implementation child, generate standalone child context without nested or contradictory parent headings, and validate every proposed child against an execution-readiness contract before writing any tracker rows. Never create a verification-only child. If the fallback cannot prove standalone scope, complete AC coverage, and safe sibling ordering, do not apply it: leave or park the parent with a durable operator_attention/decomposition event explaining why manual refinement is required. Keep writes atomic so a rejected fallback creates no partial children.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go
- cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose_test.go
- The nearest shared bead-readiness validator if reuse avoids duplicating the authoring rubric

NON-SCOPE
Do not change model/provider routing, decomposition timeout budgets, worker lifecycle visibility, or generic bead lint policy. Do not infer semantic dependencies from AC ordering when the evidence is ambiguous; use the operator-attention lane instead. Do not repair previously created children in migration code.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: none; root queue-integrity regression. Depends on ddx-2afca9c9 because this internal/agent change must pass the restored package-runtime gate.
notes:
Live deterministic-decomposition failures observed on Niflheim, 2026-07-13:
- ddx-9c3e703b was split into two implementation slices plus verification-only ddx-f3d774d3. The implementation children omitted required full-package/lefthook gates and dependencies. The operator rewrote ddx-c4497391 and ddx-03568f89, wired their dependency, and cancelled ddx-f3d774d3.
- ddx-20e2148b split fixture code from regression tripwires but omitted the dependency and full-package gate from ddx-7326dd54. The operator restored the gate and made ddx-e03399c8 depend on it.
- ddx-69672921 contained only three verification commands as its acceptance slice. A managed worker spent 14m26s and 4,137,315 tokens proving its focused regression green before the unrelated full suite timed out. The bead produced no implementation and reopened, demonstrating the direct throughput cost of verification-only children.
These are concrete production examples for TestFallbackPreClaimDecompositionRejectsVerificationOnlyChildren, TestFallbackPreClaimDecompositionProducesExecutionReadyChildren, and atomic rejection of invalid fallback output.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx production code still scans concrete harness/provider process trees and signals or reaps Fizeau-owned children based on route, harness, provider, or model facts. Fizeau owns containment for wrapped harness/provider processes, so DDx must not maintain route-aware process supervision for those descendants.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:21-40,92-240,242-478 discovers, classifies, signals, and reaps provider children using concrete route/harness facts.
- cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:42-169 and cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper_linux.go:22-113 discover and kill orphan harness processes.
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:276-297 performs route-aware child cleanup around Fizeau Execute.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1249-1258 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1616-1618 retain attempt-end and liveness integration for provider cleanup.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process.go:61-195 and cli/internal/server/workers_reap_unix.go:33-213 mix Fizeau-owned descendants into otherwise DDx-owned attempt/worker cleanup.
- Fizeau containment epic fizeau-c795e7d9 is closed, but release bead fizeau-b9a2037c must publish and prove cancellation/caller-death cleanup before DDx removes this fallback.

PROPOSED FIX
After the compatible Fizeau release from dependency fizeau-b9a2037c is pinned, delete provider-child/orphan-harness census and reaper code, route-aware child liveness checks, attempt-end provider reaping, and provider-descendant branches in generic cleanup. Keep DDx cleanup only for DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, and container processes. Add a regression test named TestDDXNeverScansOrSignalsFizeauOwnedProcesses that proves production DDx contains no provider-child/orphan-harness census and no signal/reap path keyed by harness, provider, model, or returned route facts.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, or container cleanup. Do not move bead, worktree, verification, execution-record, or container lifecycle ownership into Fizeau. Do not change Fizeau internals in this repository. Do not implement sibling child scope for provider PATH shims, __provider-launch, concrete provider-binary wrappers, or PR_SET_PDEATHSIG provider launcher removal. Do not use concrete returned route, harness, provider, or model facts to authorize a signal.

description:
PROBLEM
A single DDx attempt can monopolize the entire server-owned CPU allowance. On 2026-07-13, TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace launched five Codex providers whose aggregate use reached about 350 percent CPU, nearly saturating the installed server CPUQuota=400 percent. The aggregate service cap protected the host but provided no fairness between attempts, and a manual/offline worker outside ddx-server.service has no equivalent cap at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/server_service.go:98-102 exposes only an aggregate CPU quota and weight for the complete server-owned worker/provider/build tree. cli/internal/service/service.go:15-22 defines that policy explicitly as aggregate. cli/internal/agent/executor.go:177-188 starts each provider directly, while cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:10-29 configures only a process group and parent-death signal; no attempt-scoped CPU controller contains the provider and all descendants. Consequently one nested test/provider fanout can consume the whole managed-service budget, while the same manual worker path is unbounded.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add one attempt-scoped CPU-envelope abstraction at the provider execution boundary so the harness root and every descendant share a bounded controller. Membership must survive process-group/session changes, double-forking, and reparenting; cleanup and cancellation must act on controller membership rather than ancestry alone.
- Apply the same default and configuration to server-managed and manual/offline workers without requiring a live DDx server. Preserve the existing parent-death behavior so managed provider trees still die when their worker/server dies.
- Use a conservative default of 200 percent of one core per active attempt, allow an explicit 0 value to disable the per-attempt cap, and keep the existing aggregate server service cap as the outer ceiling.
- Emit structured attempt evidence containing requested/effective quota, controller kind, descendant membership, and fallback reason. When the platform cannot enforce a hard quota, continue with lowered scheduling priority and an operator-visible degraded-control event rather than silently claiming enforcement.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/executor.go and adjacent platform-specific executor/resource-controller files
- cli/internal/config execution settings and validation
- cli/cmd/work.go and cli/cmd/try.go only for shared configuration plumbing
- cli/internal/integration for a real descendant-fanout proof

NON-SCOPE
Do not replace or remove the aggregate ddx-server.service CPUQuota/CPUWeight policy. Do not throttle arbitrary external cargo, Go, provider, or user processes that are not descendants of the current DDx attempt. Do not require the coordination server for manual/offline execution. Do not change desired worker count, queue ordering, provider routing, or the process-group/Pdeathsig ownership contract. ddx-aa6cc320 remains responsible for removing live providers from the default test fixture.

description:
PROBLEM
During attempt 20260713T145533-c006900a, the model ran cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s, received the same host-scratch traversal failure, reran it after operator termination, and finally launched the equivalent suite through setsid -f with redirected output. The detached run entered a new session and continued consuming CPU/I/O until the operator killed it. The prompt explicitly prohibited an unchanged long-command replay, but DDx did not intervene.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2088-2094 expresses the command-fingerprint rule only as model instructions.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:39-76 keys loop detection on tool name, raw input JSON, error text, and result output. The same expensive command with a different termination message, redirection, timeout wrapper, or setsid wrapper therefore produces a different key.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:268-271 and 399-415 require four identical call-result pairs in an eight-entry window, so two or three costly replays can consume tens of minutes without firing.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:32-39 cannot reap a replay that changes session/process group; ddx-7df6b12a owns the attempt controller needed after cancellation.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an expensive-command replay detector over normalized service tool-call events. Canonicalize shell wrappers that do not change command semantics (cd into the same worktree, timeout, setsid, output redirection, foreground/background launch) while retaining command args, environment/config inputs, cwd, and a worktree/config fingerprint. After an expensive command fails, times out, or ends incomplete, cancel the attempt before a second equivalent replay unless the normalized args/environment/config or worktree fingerprint changed and the event records why the previous evidence is invalid. Persist a structured operator_attention event containing both fingerprints, outcomes, and the cancellation reason. Cancel through the ddx-7df6b12a attempt controller so detached/session-changing children are reaped.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go and adjacent replay-detector helpers/tests
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go for correlation/evidence plumbing
- attempt-controller integration introduced by ddx-7df6b12a
- execute-bead event/operator-attention mapping for replay cancellation

NON-SCOPE
Do not block distinct commands, cheap read-only commands, one legitimate validation after a code/config fingerprint change, or manual operator commands outside an attempt. Do not infer success from a killed or incomplete command. Do not lower the generic four-pair loop detector for non-expensive tools.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root reliability incident. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for controller-backed cancellation. Related to ddx-45ea2e36, which owns the independent hard attempt deadline.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-962b6108 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Production execute-bead orchestration cannot route linked-worktree or local-clone attempts through the reusable slot pool because the selected attempt backend does not carry the resolved reusable-workspace policy or worker-slot identity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) constructs linked-worktree and local-clone attempt backends without threading a reusable-workspace policy, slot pool handle, or worker-slot identity into those implementations.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` therefore receives a backend whose `Prepare(...)` method has no production-visible way to choose bounded slot allocation for eligible attempt modes.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af` and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Update `ResolveAttemptBackend` and the linked-worktree/local-clone backend constructors or option structs so they accept the resolved reusable-workspace policy, slot allocator handle, and worker-slot identity. Keep Docker backend construction unchanged except for any no-op plumbing needed by shared interfaces. Add focused tests proving both eligible backend types receive the policy and slot identity used later by preparation.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestResolveAttemptBackendThreadsReusableWorkspacePolicy` proves `ResolveAttemptBackend` passes the resolved reusable-workspace policy and worker-slot identity into linked-worktree and local-clone backend instances.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx attempt policy can still change based on route/provider/model identity or provider-shaped failure strings, which makes policy behavior depend on audit metadata instead of typed Fizeau lifecycle inputs plus DDx-owned evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_failure.go:77-199 classifies provider failures by matching provider-specific text and route-shaped failures. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go:104-242 folds status, exit code, and error text into failure-mode decisions. Phase 1 WB-1 requires DDx to preserve route identity as audit evidence while making route-neutral policy decisions from typed Fizeau lifecycle data: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:128-143.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the new DDx attempt-policy adapter tests and data model so harness, provider, model, and route are treated as audit fields only. Identical typed lifecycle inputs plus identical DDx-owned evidence must return identical decisions even when route identity differs. Keep provider identity available for reports and diagnostics, but prevent it from participating in the decision key.

NON-SCOPE
Do not select a harness, provider, model, or route. Do not parse Fizeau stderr. Do not make Fizeau own bead state, review policy, landing, or closure. Do not delete all legacy text tables in this bead except where needed to route the new adapter. Fizeau internal routing, provider selection, provider retry, and provider-specific protocols remain non-scope. Review content, direct provider integration in DDx, timeboxed DDx bypasses, direct-provider fallback, and Fizeau demotion/replacement are non-scope. Do not implement execute-bead report wiring in this child.

PARENT
Preserve parent reference ddx-b8cacbeb. Source decomposition parent field: ddx-66a8883f.

DEPS
Depends on the child bead that pins the compatible Fizeau typed lifecycle contract and on the child bead that adds the typed Fizeau attempt-decision adapter. Preserve upstream dependency IDs fizeau#fizeau-8440f9ec and fizeau#fizeau-9d2c83e8. Preserve governing WB-1 references to fizeau#fizeau-6f9ffa71, fizeau#fizeau-c795e7d9, and fizeau#fizeau-022cbb9a.

description:
PROBLEM
With the slot pool, reuse/scrub path, and preserved build state implemented in the sibling children, the production execute-bead path still prepares a throwaway workspace per attempt and defers destructive cleanup, so no real bead benefits and operators have no visibility into whether reuse is happening or what it saves.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares a workspace with `attemptBackend.Prepare(...)` for every attempt and installs a `defer` that ends in `_ = attemptBackend.Cleanup(ctx, workspace)`, treating the workspace as disposable; the only preservation branch is `runtime.PreserveAttemptWorktree` for the worktree backend.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` (`WriteExecutionCleanupMetadata`) writes per-attempt metadata into the workspace, which must be scrubbed on reuse rather than carried into the next bead.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) constructs backends without any pool handle or worker-slot identity, so orchestration has nothing to thread through.
- No hit/miss or savings counters exist anywhere in the attempt path, so there is no signal that would have surfaced the Niflheim cold-build amplification (roughly 20-24 minutes per bead in cold lefthook/clippy runs).

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Thread the resolved reusable-workspace policy and worker-slot identity from `ResolveAttemptBackend` into both the linked-worktree and local-clone backends so production preparation goes through the bounded slot allocator. Replace the unconditional destructive cleanup in the `execute_bead.go` defer with a release that returns a healthy slot to the pool and only deletes on quarantine, while preserving existing `PreserveAttemptWorktree`, `KeepOnError`, evidence-preservation, and the `resource_exhausted` classification of `Prepare` failures. Emit reuse telemetry — slot hit/miss counts plus time and bytes saved — through the existing execution event/observability path so operators can see reuse behaviour per project and worker.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
During autonomous drain on eitri (2026-08-04/05), ddx work --watch workers repeatedly entered phase=server.unavailable with message "server unreachable: holding queue until /api/health returns" while curl https://127.0.0.1:7743/api/health returned {"status":"ok"}. Steward had to kill/restart workers 3+ times in one babysit window after land/pre-commit attempts (especially RC8 go-test -race ./cmd). One bead-scoped failure must not park the entire worker indefinitely when the coordination server is healthy (P4 blast radius, P10 self-unstick).

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
1. Resume probe couples liveness to agent smoke, not health:
   cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:353-389 serverHealthProbe GETs /api/health then requires agent.RunWithConfigViaService(... Prompt: "server health smoke test") ExitCode==0. If health is OK but smoke fails (routing, provider, transient LLM error), Healthy returns false forever.
2. Watch loop holds claims while serverOutage.Active() (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2182-2226) and only clears on probe true.
3. Outage activation can fire from report text / no-viable-provider thresholds (cli/internal/agent/server_outage.go:91-122, isServerTransportFailureText:148-161) after non-transport land failures; recovery then depends on the over-strict smoke probe.

Observed: after ddx-dee23a4d / ddx-49e799f9 task_succeeded + long pre-commit, workers stuck server.unavailable despite /api/health ok until process restart.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Split probes: liveness for resume = /api/health HTTP 200 only (or health + optional cheap non-LLM smoke). Do not require a Fizeau Execute success to clear server.unavailable.
2. Optionally keep a separate degraded-routing signal that does not claim "server unreachable" or hold the queue on health-ok hosts.
3. On Activate, log the report detail that triggered outage (bead_id, failure snippet) so false positives are diagnosable.
4. Tests: TestServerHealthProbeResumesOnHealthOKWithoutAgentSmoke; TestServerOutageDoesNotActivateOnPreCommitPackageFailureText (if currently matched).

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove server outage handling for real TLS/transport failures. Do not demote thrashing beads. Do not disable pre-commit.

reliability P4/P10; FEAT-010 work loop stay-alive.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still chooses or biases concrete Fizeau routes in production even after removing the obvious run/try/work preflight. Local harness-name dispatch, lifecycle profile discovery, server defaults, project-model inheritance, and dead exported route-control APIs let DDx select harness/provider/model/profile policy it does not own. Removing preflight also left the advertised 60s route-resolution lease guard disconnected.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:90-135, cli/internal/agent/dispatch.go:36-67, and cli/internal/agent/runner.go:84-114 route virtual/script names into DDx-local runners instead of forwarding an operator harness constraint to Fizeau.
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:477-494,559-579 and cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:237-247 call ListPolicies/ListModels and select concrete lifecycle profiles.
- cli/internal/server/graphql_adapters.go:73-100, workers_supervisor.go:23-106, graphql/resolver_feat008.go:89-120, and the workers frontend seed default/smart profiles; server workers.go:363-372 and agent/run_dispatch_spec.go:103-127 leave opaque passthrough false, so config/resolved.go:73-80 can inject project agent.model into an unpinned request.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6935-7533, service_run.go:461-636, cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go:104-379, internal/agent/escalation/ladder.go, and model_discovery_containment.go retain exclusion, resolver, catalog-ladder, historical-route-seeding, and discovery-control capabilities.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:88-91,215-228 plus work/try/server flag plumbing retain route-resolution-timeout after deleting its resolver call, making the documented lease-release guard a no-op.

PROPOSED FIX
Route every production agent and lifecycle invocation through Fizeau. Preserve explicit operator Harness, Provider, Model, Policy/Profile, MaxPower, and other public passthrough byte-for-byte, but never synthesize concrete route fields. Express DDx-owned difficulty or escalation only through abstract MinPower. Remove local script/virtual name dispatch from production, lifecycle catalog/profile selection, default/smart profile injection, project-model inheritance for opaque execution entry points, route exclusion/catalog/seed machinery, and dead exported control APIs. Retain the 60s wedge guard by timing only Fizeau's opaque route stage from Execute dispatch until its first routing_decision event; on expiry cancel the operation, release the lease, and append operator_attention, and permanently disarm the timer once routing_decision arrives.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove read-only provider/model inventory or UI display of Fizeau-returned route evidence, change Fizeau internals, reject explicit operator passthrough, implement typed-result policy that requires a newer Fizeau release, or implement reviewer cardinality/stronger-review policy owned by dependent beads.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
None; Phase 1 WB-2a is start-immediately and this bead is the execution-boundary prerequisite for difficulty and review work.
notes: ADVERSARIAL PROOF REQUIREMENTS (2026-07-15): remove post-Execute ListHarnesses billing lookup and all ListModels/ListPolicies/profile/model/catalog inspection from run/try/work/server control. Forward opaque harness/profile/model/provider/policy passthrough byte-for-byte (no agent->fiz alias rewrite or trimming). Abstract MinPower escalation must honor MaxPower and stop without dispatch when no strictly higher valid bound exists. Implement exact TestEscalationRaisesOnlyMinPowerWithoutCatalogLookup with whole-attempt tripwires for ListHarnesses, ListModels, ListPolicies, ResolveRoute, and profile selection; strengthen try delegation to assert command success.

description:
PROBLEM
Reused attempts must emit the same combined reusable workspace telemetry payload shape as cold-start attempts while carrying hit-oriented allocation data and non-zero savings when the savings estimator reports them. Today reused-attempt allocation and savings signals are assembled on a separate path, so the event shape can diverge from cold starts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` handles reusable workspace preparation and cleanup but does not guarantee reused attempts emit through the same normalized combined payload path as cold-start attempts.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` exposes reusable workspace outcome metadata, but reused allocation outcome and savings metadata are not consistently normalized into the shared combined payload shape.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace savings for reused attempts", child "attempt-backend: define combined reusable workspace telemetry payload", child "attempt-backend: emit combined reusable workspace telemetry for cold starts", and child "attempt-backend: carry reused workspace savings into combined telemetry inputs". Route reused-attempt combined reusable workspace telemetry through the normalized combined payload builder or equivalent shared emission path. Reused attempts must report the shared event name, the shared field set, hit values appropriate to allocation reuse, and the time-saved and bytes-saved values delivered by the reusable workspace savings contract.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Parent bead `ddx-54ff73df`: attempt-backend combined workspace hit, miss, and savings telemetry.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not change the existing Docker attempt backend shared-cache behaviour while adding this event.

description:
PROBLEM
When a work/try attempt exceeds the active-attempt wall-clock budget, the worker must not leave the bead leased or stall the queue. The niflheim incident required operator intervention to release the lease and stop resource consumption.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3524-3539 installs only the phase-empty progress watchdog for the attempt lifetime and does not enforce a hard active-attempt deadline that releases the lease.
- cli/internal/agent/work/watchdog.go:49-80 treats populated harness/model/route activity as healthy, so lease release is not triggered for a routed but unproductive attempt.

PROPOSED FIX
When the active-attempt wall-clock budget expires, cancel the attempt, release its lease, append operator_attention with bead ID, attempt ID, elapsed time, configured budget, and last activity, and continue draining ready queue work. Add or update operator-attention rendering/tests for the new timeout reason.

NON-SCOPE
Do not shorten the generic ddx run three-hour provider cap. Do not change queue ordering, provider routing, the phase-empty watchdog, or long-running bead acceptance commands. Do not rely on process ancestry alone. Do not implement sibling populated-route, manual/server parity, or descendant-reaping behavior except where needed for lease release on wall-clock expiry.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-45ea2e36. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for attempt-controller members. Governing reliability incident: niflheim-active-route-wedge; cross-reference ddx-8a78ee90.

acceptance:
1. TestServerOutageActivationLogsTriggerDetail proves activation output includes bead_id when provided, a reason, and a bounded failure snippet or matched signal.
2. TestServerOutageActivationLogSnippetIsBounded, or an equivalent named TestServerOutage* symbol, proves long report text is truncated or bounded in diagnostics.

4. cd cli && go test ./cmd/ ./internal/agent/ -run 'TestServerHealthProbe|TestServerOutage' -count=1 passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
When server.unavailable activates, operators cannot reliably tell which bead-scoped failure or report text caused the queue-wide hold. That made the eitri false-server-unavailable incident harder to diagnose after ddx-dee23a4d / ddx-49e799f9 task_succeeded and long pre-commit activity. This child owns the activation observability portion of parent bead ddx-96fae203.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/server_outage.go:91-122 activates outage state from report text / no-viable-provider thresholds, but the activation path does not persist or log enough trigger detail such as bead_id and the failure snippet that matched. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2182-2226 then holds claims while serverOutage.Active() and only clears on a healthy probe, leaving limited evidence for false positives.

PROPOSED FIX
When server outage state activates, include structured diagnostic detail in the existing log/report path: bead_id when available, activation reason, and a bounded failure snippet or matched signal. Keep snippets short and avoid leaking unrelated large logs. Use this evidence to distinguish true server transport failures from bead-scoped failures during future incidents.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove server outage handling for real TLS/transport failures. Do not demote thrashing beads. Do not disable pre-commit. Do not change health probe semantics or outage classification except where needed to expose the existing trigger reason. Preserve governing artifact references: reliability P4/P10; FEAT-010 work loop stay-alive. Preserve parent/dependency references: parent bead ddx-96fae203 and governing parent ddx-b79130f2.

description:
PROBLEM
After an execution provider exits with task_failed and leaves implementation edits, DDx synthesizes an iteration commit. That commit runs the repository pre-commit hook even though the provider already ran or failed the same gate. On 2026-07-13, the failed ddx-0f29e87a attempt entered the internal/agent race suite a second time during synthesis and recreated real Codex provider processes, consuming CPU and preventing prompt failure finalization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1297-1383 invokes GitOps.SynthesizeCommit whenever the attempt worktree is dirty and HEAD did not move, including when exitCode is non-zero and the preliminary outcome is task_failed. cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:151-180 stages the implementation diff and executes plain git commit -m, so repository hooks run inside DDx orchestration. The durable DDx audit paths already use --no-verify at cli/internal/agent/durable_audit.go:125-128 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1724-1731, demonstrating the intended separation between orchestration-owned commits and user-invoked validation.

PROPOSED FIX
Make RealGitOps.SynthesizeCommit create the DDx-owned synthesized attempt commit without invoking repository hooks. Preserve the substantive dirty diff and the per-attempt commit-message/audit contract. Keep validation in the provider run and DDx gate/review pipeline; do not silently reinterpret a failed attempt as success.

NON-SCOPE
Do not skip provider-requested gates, landing gates, or operator git hooks. Do not discard failed implementation edits or rewrite existing execute-bead history. Do not weaken test assertions or timeouts.

Preserve explicit worktree support for operators whose sandbox contract permits writes to the primary repository Git metadata. Update public config/docs to describe the sandbox requirement and add proofs for default selection and a commit from a clone-contained Git directory.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-e69080a9 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Reusable attempt workspaces need a post-reset integrity gate. If reset/scrub fails to prove the workspace is clean, DDx must quarantine the slot instead of returning unsafe state to the reusable pool. Healthy slots should still be returned to the pool after successful cleanup.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- There is no reset/scrub integrity failure path in `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go`, so unsafe reusable state would otherwise be indistinguishable from healthy reusable state.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) currently remove workspaces rather than validating reusable slot health before reuse.

PROPOSED FIX
Add post-reset/scrub integrity validation for reusable slots in both linked-worktree and local-clone cleanup paths. A failed integrity check must quarantine the slot, prevent future reuse, and emit operator-visible diagnostics containing slot, backend, project, and reason. A successful cleanup and integrity check must return only healthy slots to the pool for future sequential reuse.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this child concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement repository identity mismatch, cleanup-failure quarantine, or live-process quarantine behavior except as minimal fixtures needed for integrity/healthy-return coverage.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/...` passes.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` passes on the final staged tree.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

title: tighten server outage activation and log the triggering failure

acceptance:
1. TestFizeauV015ModuleContract or renamed successor TestFizeauCompatibleModuleContract proves github.com/easel/fizeau resolves to the pinned compatible public release with no replace directive and no pseudo-version.
2. TestFizeauCompatibleModuleContract verifies the pinned version satisfies the public release prerequisite for fizeau#fizeau-8440f9ec and, where exposed by the release, fizeau#fizeau-9d2c83e8 typed cause/stage detail.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "Test(FizeauV015ModuleContract|FizeauCompatibleModuleContract)" -count=1 passes.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
DDx attempt policy cannot safely consume a stable Fizeau lifecycle result while cli/go.mod may resolve github.com/easel/fizeau to a release, pseudo-version, or replace directive that does not provide the public CONTRACT-003 lifecycle surfaces required by DDx.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The Phase 1 WB-1 artifact requires DDx to consume Fizeau CONTRACT-003 typed immediate errors and final events before WB-1-dependent DDx work proceeds: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146. The DDx CLI currently pins github.com/easel/fizeau in cli/go.mod:7, and the existing module-boundary proof only asserts the older v0.15-style contract in cli/internal/agent/fizeau_v015_module_contract_test.go:13-17.

PROPOSED FIX
Update or preserve cli/go.mod and cli/go.sum so github.com/easel/fizeau resolves to the first compatible public release satisfying fizeau#fizeau-8440f9ec and the applicable typed detail from fizeau#fizeau-9d2c83e8. Extend or rename the module contract test so DDx proves the dependency is a tagged public compatible release, with no replace directive and no pseudo-version.

NON-SCOPE
Do not select a harness, provider, model, or route. Do not parse Fizeau stderr. Do not make Fizeau own bead state, review policy, landing, or closure. Do not implement DDx attempt retry/escalation decisions in this bead. Do not delete DDx provider text tables in this bead. Fizeau internal routing, provider selection, provider retry, and provider-specific protocols remain non-scope. Review content, direct provider integration in DDx, timeboxed DDx bypasses, direct-provider fallback, and Fizeau demotion/replacement are non-scope.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
Blocked by fizeau#fizeau-8440f9ec. Depends on fizeau#fizeau-9d2c83e8 for typed cause/stage detail. Preserve governing WB-1 dependencies on fizeau#fizeau-6f9ffa71, fizeau#fizeau-c795e7d9, and fizeau#fizeau-022cbb9a for applicable CONTRACT-003 children and the boundary conformance suite.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx pins Fizeau v0.14.50, whose subprocess discovery refresher discards its bounded context and whose Codex model discovery launches ptyquota with context.Background. A cancelled DDx request or stopped server can therefore return while codex --no-alt-screen continues consuming CPU and writing caller-owned temp/cache state. DDx-side containment wrappers reduce symptoms but do not repair the dependency lifecycle.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/go.mod:7 pins github.com/easel/fizeau v0.14.50.
- In that release, Fizeau internal/serviceimpl/subprocess_discovery_cache.go:74-94 ignores the discoverycache.Refresher context before calling DefaultModelSnapshot.
- In that release, Fizeau internal/harnesses/codex/model_discovery.go:20-48 calls ptyquota.Run(context.Background(), ...).
- cli/cmd/lifecycle_model_discovery_test.go proves DDx's outer containment helper, but a local wrapper test cannot prove the Fizeau cache refresher or PTY receives cancellation.

PROPOSED FIX
Wait for upstream fizeau-d25b2862 to add a context-aware model-discovery contract, pass the refresh context through subprocessDiscoveryRefresher, and reap the Codex PTY on cancellation. After an upstream release contains that closing commit, bump cli/go.mod and cli/go.sum to that release. Add DDx integration coverage proving the service lifecycle cancellation reaches dependency discovery, returns only after the probe is reaped, and produces no late cache/home writes. Verify the existing embedded dispatch temp-root regressions with the released dependency.

IN-SCOPE FILES

- cli/go.sum
- cli/cmd/lifecycle_model_discovery_test.go and the nearest DDx service-lifecycle integration fixture

NON-SCOPE

description:
PROBLEM
DDx estimates missing cost from concrete model and harness identity, accepts its own local price input, and stores execution cost in a value-only field. That makes absent cost indistinguishable from explicit zero and presents DDx guesses as accounting facts. Cost must be only the value Fizeau reported, with explicit presence preserved from execution through indexing, metrics, CLI, and GraphQL.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/pricing.go:3-35 owns DDx model pricing and EstimateCost. cli/cmd/usage_support.go:54-72 and cli/internal/processmetrics/processmetrics.go:1274-1323 estimate missing cost from route identity. cli/internal/config/types.go:319-322 still accepts DDx local_per_1k_tokens pricing. cli/internal/agent/types.go:106-133 defines Result.CostUSD as value-only. cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:324-346 copies final cost only when greater than zero. cli/internal/agent/session_index.go:22-40 has CostPresent but lines 206-221 and 240-293 synthesize it from nonzero values. cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go:818-820 drops explicit zero.

PROPOSED FIX
Delete cli/internal/agent/pricing.go, EstimateCost, DDx local price configuration, and every model/provider/harness identity cost estimate. Add explicit cost presence at agent.Result and translate the public Fizeau terminal contract exactly: nil is unknown, non-nil 0.0 is known zero, and non-nil positive is known positive. Preserve that distinction through session writes/reindex, usage and process metrics, and GraphQL. Historical records without presence remain unknown. Aggregates sum only present values and expose unknown participation instead of fabricating a complete total.

NON-SCOPE
Do not classify billing mode, add a replacement DDx price table or remote pricing lookup, reinterpret missing as zero/free, change Fizeau pricing, or use reported cost for routing, retry, escalation, review grading, admission, or close policy. Fizeau predicted candidate cost remains audit evidence and is not DDx pricing.

description:
PROBLEM

description:
PROBLEM
Thrashing beads such as ddx-6e971b9e repeat repair cycles at the same requested_min_power after review_fixable_gap, so the second implementer pass can reproduce the same partial AC failure and exhaust repair budget.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:163 requires capability-sensitive failures, including review block / fixable gap, to record retry_power with only MinPower raised when policy permits.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:710 says failed checks, review_fixable_gap, and similar capability-sensitive outcomes schedule a higher-power retry by raising the next request's MinPower.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:616 says review_fixable_gap within repair_max_cycles currently emits repair-cycle-started and runs append-only repair in the same workspace.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1167 exposes EscalationNextFloor only for the no-changes smart-retry path, leaving the repair-cycle path without a MinPower floor raise before the next implementer dispatch.

PROPOSED FIX
On review classification review_fixable_gap with repair budget remaining and a higher abstract MinPower available, record a retry_power decision, raise only the abstract MinPower floor for the next implementer attempt/cycle, and emit power-escalation-requested with prior_min_power, next_min_power, and reason=review_fixable_gap. Preserve operator passthrough, MaxPower, dependency metadata, governing artifact references, and result evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not pick concrete models/providers/routes; Fizeau owns that. Do not raise MinPower for Fizeau transport/auth/quota typed outcomes. Do not demote thrashing beads. Do not land without APPROVE. Do not implement reframe/decomposer content.

3. TestExecuteBeadLoopStoreDoesNotExposeConcreteStore passes and proves execute-loop dependencies can be satisfied without naming *bead.Store outside test construction helpers.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/server/... ./internal/escalation/... passes.

description:
PROBLEM
TD-027 §21 requires the agent and server layers to compile against bead interface contracts before storage concretes are relocated. These packages still have many *bead.Store test fixtures, helper wrappers, and production escape hatches that make the later internal-package move too broad and fragile.

ROOT CAUSE with file:line
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:1580 accepts *bead.Store in staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/ddxroot_paths.go:12 returns *bead.Store from projectBeadStore.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_mutation_beads.go:14 returns *bead.Store from mutationResolver.beadStore.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go:199 type-asserts a store back to *bead.Store.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:5896 documents deterministic ready-queue eligibility as bead.Store-specific instead of depending on an interface.
- Many agent/server test helpers still return *bead.Store, which prevents a package-level AST proof from staying small.

PROPOSED FIX
Update agent, agent/try, server, and server/graphql production code and test helpers to accept bead.Backend, bead.ReadOnlyBackend, or existing narrow sub-interfaces where the concrete is not required. Introduce local test-only fakes/adapters where a test currently embeds *bead.Store only to satisfy a small method set. Preserve concrete construction only at the package boundary where NewStore/NewStoreWithCollection is called.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change command/metrics caller clusters assigned to the sibling caller-narrowing child.
- Do not move storage concrete definitions or aliases.
- Do not relocate lifecycle WatcherHub.
- Do not change queue semantics, claim semantics, retry policy, worker lifecycle policy, or GraphQL behavior except for type narrowing.
- Do not implement per-concern L/C/X/Q/D/A/MIG behavior or AxonStore/AxonBackend behavior.
- Do not manually edit .ddx/beads.jsonl.
- Do not fix unrelated provider-launch/orphan integration flakes; if cd cli && go test ./... is blocked by pre-existing failures, report exact failing Test* names and leave this child’s changes otherwise verified.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
- TD-027 §21 Module Boundary / Boundary Lockdown.

PARENT/DEPS
- Parent: ddx-74452926.
- Must be scheduled after foundation ddx-c6317784 and the per-concern dependency beads already referenced by the parent, including ddx-3af1c1a6, ddx-71d3a2de, ddx-0ab16765, and Axon follow-up ddx-9c5bca8f where applicable.

description: PROBLEM: on 2026-07-06..2026-07-19 two ddx drains of telepathdata/cayce silently forked the repo: one checkout had branch.master.merge=refs/heads/main while the repo default was refs/heads/master, so each worker fleet pushed commits AND the beads.jsonl tracker to a different remote branch for 13 days. Because the tracker lives in git, forking the branch forks the queue itself — both sides showed healthy progress, duplicated ~100 non-chore commits of work under different bead IDs, and nobody was alerted. Recovered manually on 2026-07-20 (archive branch + delete + port-audit bead cayce-30ea87db). ROOT CAUSE: ddx work/try honor whatever upstream the checkout is configured with and have no preflight check that the branch being drained is (or descends from) the remote's default branch (origin/HEAD). PROPOSED FIX: before claiming the first bead, ddx work (and ddx try) resolve origin/HEAD and compare with the current branch's upstream: hard-fail with a clear message when the upstream ref names a different branch than origin/HEAD (override flag, e.g. --allow-non-default-branch, for deliberate feature-branch drains); also warn when the local branch is behind its upstream at drain start. NON-SCOPE

description:
PROBLEM
Running the required cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... gate launches five real Codex provider processes from TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace. In the 2026-07-13 ddx-2502d3c6 attempt, the package test spawned PIDs 225004, 225054, 225173, 225576, and 226111 as __provider-launch ... codex exec; each ran for more than six minutes at about 10-12% CPU. The test package approached its 10-minute timeout, blocking the single queue worker and consuming server-cgroup CPU for a test whose stated concern is only parent-repo Git serialization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:31-55 builds five production NewRunner(Config{}) instances and labels directive-file paths as model names under the obsolete script route. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:73-89 then calls ExecuteBeadWithConfig concurrently with those production runners. The current service-backed runner resolves the request to Codex, so each directive path is passed to codex exec as -m instead of being consumed by a hermetic script fixture. The test comments at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:35-37 explicitly say agent output is irrelevant. The package previously had to be repaired for the same 600-second budget under ddx-1a0d4d26, but this fixture has regressed into live provider execution.

- Replace the five production runners in this Git-lock regression with an explicit bounded hermetic AgentRunner fixture that returns the minimal no-changes result needed to reach and validate pre-dispatch serialization.
- Preserve the real temporary Git repository, five concurrent ExecuteBeadWithConfig calls, tracker commits, worktree creation, and HEAD CAS assertions.

- Ensure subprocesses are canceled and reaped on test failure or timeout.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production provider discovery, reduce the concurrency below five, delete the HEAD race assertions, or skip the test. Live provider integration remains build-tagged/explicit integration coverage, not part of the default package gate.

None.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx production code still installs provider-binary PATH shims and exposes a hidden direct provider launch wrapper even though Fizeau owns provider process containment. This keeps DDx crossing the Fizeau/DDx boundary by preparing concrete provider execution instead of only calling Fizeau Execute with a cancellable context.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:93-102,116-128 installs a route/provider shim in PATH before invoking Fizeau Execute.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:13-56,100-179 defines the hidden provider wrapper contract and concrete provider binary shim behavior.
- cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:12-70 exposes the hidden provider launch command.
- cli/cmd/provider_launch_unix.go and cli/cmd/provider_launch_windows.go implement platform-specific direct provider exec/PDEATHSIG behavior.
- Fizeau containment epic fizeau-c795e7d9 is closed, but release bead fizeau-b9a2037c must publish and prove cancellation/caller-death cleanup before DDx removes this fallback.

PROPOSED FIX
After the compatible Fizeau release from dependency fizeau-b9a2037c is pinned, remove DDx provider PATH shim installation, the provider_spawn wrapper code, the __provider-launch command, and platform launcher implementations. Add a regression test named TestDDXNeverInstallsProviderShimOrLaunchWrapper that inspects production code paths and fails if DDx can still install a provider shim, expose __provider-launch, maintain a concrete provider-binary wrapper, or configure PR_SET_PDEATHSIG for a provider launcher. DDx must retain only cancellation of the context supplied to Fizeau Execute for Fizeau-owned provider trees.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, or container cleanup. Do not move bead, worktree, verification, execution-record, or container lifecycle ownership into Fizeau. Do not change Fizeau internals in this repository. Do not implement sibling child scope for provider-child/orphan-harness scanning, route-aware liveness, attempt-end provider reap, or provider-descendant cleanup branches. Do not use concrete returned route, harness, provider, or model facts to authorize a signal.

    # collection lock and deadlocks until LockWait (cascading CI "bead: lock
    # timeout" failures). Flag nested WriteAll on *bead.Store; use WriteAllLocked.
    lock-reentry-lint:
      <<: *go_checks
      name: "Lock re-entry lint (WriteAll inside WithLock)"
      glob: "cli/**/*.go"
      run: |
        staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR | grep -E '^cli/.+\.go$' || true)
        [ -z "$staged" ] && exit 0
        pkgs=$(printf '%s\n' "$staged" | xargs -n1 dirname | sort -u | sed 's|^cli/|./|' | grep -v '/testdata/' | grep -v '^\./tools/lint/lockreentrylint' || true)
        [ -z "$pkgs" ] && exit 0
        out=$(go run ./tools/lint/lockreentrylint/cmd/lockreentrylint $pkgs 2>&1) || true
        violations=""
        for f in $staged; do
          bare="${f#cli/}"
          m=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep "/$bare:" || true)
          if [ -n "$m" ]; then
            violations="$violations$m"$'\n'
          fi
        done
        if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
          printf '%s' "$violations"
          exit 1
        fi
        exit 0
      skip:
        - merge
        - rebase
      fail_text: "Store.WriteAll nested inside WithLock re-enters the non-reentrant collection lock. Use WriteAllLocked (ddx-2a319f04)."

    # Go tests - targeted testing
    go-test:
      <<: *go_checks
      name: "Go Tests"
      glob: "cli/**/*.go"
      run: sh ../scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh {staged_files}
      skip:
        - merge
        - rebase
      env:
        CGO_ENABLED: "1"
        SKIP_INTEGRATION_TESTS: "true"

    # Secrets scanning - prefer gitleaks when available
    secrets:
      <<: *security_checks
      name: "Scan for secrets"
      run: |
        if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          gitleaks protect --staged --verbose --redact
        else
          # Fallback to staged-added-line pattern matching when gitleaks is absent.
          # Scanning whole tracker JSONL files causes noisy false positives on prose.
          added_lines=$(git diff --cached --unified=0 --no-color -- {staged_files} | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++')

          patterns='((api[_-]?key|apikey|secret|password|passwd|pwd|credential|private[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|auth[_-]?token)[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*["'"'"'][A-Za-z0-9_./+=-]{20,})|(Authorization:[[:space:]]*Bearer[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,})'
          if printf '%s\n' "$added_lines" | grep -E "$patterns"; then
            echo "Potential secrets detected"
            exit 1
          fi

          # AWS keys
          if printf '%s\n' "$added_lines" | grep -E 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}'; then
            echo "AWS key pattern detected"
            exit 1
          fi

          # GitHub tokens
          if printf '%s\n' "$added_lines" | grep -E 'ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}'; then
            echo "GitHub token pattern detected"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
      exclude:
        - "*.md"
        - "go.sum"
        - "package-lock.json"
        - "*_test.go"
        - "**/dist/**"
        - "scripts/test-secrets-fallback.sh"
      fail_text: "Secrets detected! Remove them or add to .gitleaks.toml if false positive"

    # Binary and large file check
    large-files:
      name: "Check file sizes"
      run: |
        for file in {staged_files}; do
          size=$(stat -f%z "$file" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
          if [ "$size" -gt 5242880 ]; then
            echo "Large file detected: $file ($(($size / 1048576))MB)"
            exit 1
          fi
        done
      exclude:
        - "*.png"
        - "*.jpg"
        - "*.jpeg"
        - "*.gif"
        - "*.svg"
        - "*.ico"
        - "*.pdf"
        - "*.woff"
        - "*.woff2"
        - "*.ttf"
        - "*.eot"
        # bead store grows monotonically with queue activity; expected to exceed 5MB
        - ".ddx/beads.jsonl"
        # archive partner accumulates closed beads forever; trends past 5MB
        - ".ddx/beads-archive.jsonl"
      fail_text: "Large files detected. Use Git LFS for files over 5MB"

    # DDx validation - only when relevant files change
    ddx-validate:
      name: "Validate DDx"
      run: |
        # Only run if DDx files are staged
        if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qE '(\.ddx\.yml|templates/|patterns/|prompts/)'; then
          exit 0
        fi

        # Strip git's local-env-vars before invoking ddx so any git commands
        # the ddx process spawns honor cmd.Dir / -C <dir> rather than the
        # GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / etc. inherited from this hook's context.
        # Without this, ddx's git invocations mutate THIS repo (the hook's),
        # producing core.bare=true and stray core.worktree corruption.
        # ddx-64ac553a Phase 0 (defensive triage; real fix is the central
        # git.Command wrapper in Phase 2a).
        unset $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)

        # Collect staged paths and pass them to --paths so doctor only validates
        # the checks relevant to the staged files (config or resource), skipping
        # global installation checks (e.g. legacy skill symlinks) that are
        # unrelated to the content of the staged change. [ddx-777f4a09]
        staged_paths="$(git diff --cached --name-only | tr '\n' ' ')"

        # Check for DDx command availability
        if command -v ddx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ddx doctor --paths "$staged_paths" >/dev/null 2>&1
        elif [ -x "./cli/ddx" ]; then
          ./cli/ddx doctor --paths "$staged_paths" >/dev/null 2>&1
        fi
      fail_text: "DDx validation failed. Run 'ddx doctor' for details"

      run: |

        done
        exit $failed
