description:
PROBLEM
Even after reusable slot state exists, production execute-bead preparation still treats each linked-worktree or local-clone attempt as a disposable workspace, so real executions do not use the bounded project-local slot allocator.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` calls `attemptBackend.Prepare(...)` directly for every attempt and treats the returned workspace as a disposable per-attempt workspace.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` currently resolves backends without a production path that binds linked-worktree/local-clone preparation to the reusable slot allocator.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, on the child that threads reusable workspace policy through backend resolution, and on the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Change the linked-worktree and local-clone production preparation path so, when reuse is enabled, `Prepare(...)` acquires the bounded slot for the resolved worker-slot identity and returns a prepared workspace rooted in that slot. Ensure the existing attempt metadata and evidence provenance still point to the concrete attempt workspace path used for execution.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
Even with a correct shared scrub routine, reusable attempt workspaces remain unsafe unless both attempt backends invoke it before handing an existing slot to a new bead.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` prepare fresh attempt directories today and therefore have no pre-handoff reuse scrub call.
- Cleanup paths in `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` delete workspaces after use, so backend prepare flows currently rely on directory creation/deletion instead of a reusable-slot hygiene contract.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` writes cleanup metadata that would persist when the backend reuses a slot unless prepare invokes the shared scrub routine first.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire both existing attempt backend prepare flows to call the shared reusable-workspace scrub routine before returning a reused workspace slot for a new bead. Pass the requested base revision and allocator-owned allowlist into the scrub routine, propagate integrity-check failures as reuse refusal, and leave backend-specific slot acquisition to the sibling allocator/config child.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Parent container: `ddx-bb1410e1`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.

- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement backend-specific slot acquisition beyond calling the shared scrub routine from existing backend prepare flows.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.

Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.

description:
PROBLEM
Every bead attempt creates a fresh checkout and deletes it on cleanup, so identical sequential work on the same project pays full setup cost each time and discards all local state. Making a workspace survive between beads is only safe if DDx can prove the next bead sees exactly its requested base revision with no residue from the previous bead, and can refuse reuse when it cannot prove that.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare`) creates a linked worktree at a fresh attempt-specific path via `gitOps.WorktreeAdd`, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) unconditionally runs `WorktreeRemove`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare`) runs a full `git clone` plus `checkout --detach` for every attempt, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) deletes the whole clone with `os.RemoveAll`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) documents that local-clone is the sandbox-safe default, so the default path is the one paying full clone cost per bead.
- There is no reset/scrub path anywhere in `attempt_backend.go`: because the directory is always new, no code establishes that staged changes, modified tracked files, untracked files, evidence under `.ddx/executions/`, environment-derived credentials, or cleanup metadata written by `WriteExecutionCleanupMetadata` (`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031`) are absent.

PROPOSED FIX
Build on the slot allocator from the sibling bead "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface" (DEPENDS ON that child; do not start until its allocator and config land). Teach both `WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare` and `LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare` to request a slot, and when a healthy slot with a matching repository identity already exists, reset it to the requested base revision instead of recreating it: hard-reset tracked state, scrub staged and modified files, remove untracked files including evidence directories and attempt cleanup metadata, drop environment-derived credential material, and preserve only explicitly allowlisted paths. Verify repository identity before reuse and fall back to a fresh workspace on mismatch. description:
PROBLEM
A reusable attempt workspace that fails cleanup or still has descendant processes after an attempt is unsafe to return to the healthy pool. DDx needs a refusal path that quarantines that slot and surfaces operator-visible diagnostics.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) currently removes linked-worktree workspaces rather than tracking reusable slot health, quarantine state, or reuse eligibility.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) currently removes local-clone workspaces rather than tracking reusable slot health, quarantine state, or reuse eligibility.
- There is no reusable-slot descendant-process refusal path in `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go`, so live processes would otherwise be indistinguishable from a clean reusable slot.

PROPOSED FIX
During cleanup for both attempt backends, detect cleanup failures and surviving descendant processes. Mark the affected reusable slot quarantined, remove it from the healthy reusable pool, and emit operator-visible diagnostics containing slot, backend, project, and quarantine reason. A quarantined slot must never be reused by later attempts.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this child concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement repository identity mismatch or post-reset integrity quarantine behavior except as minimal fixtures needed for cleanup/live-process coverage.

acceptance:
1. TestImporter_Verify_DetectsDrift covers verifyImportedAxonCorpus returning an error after post-import target mutation; the error names the drifted bead ID and indicates the specific field drift.
2. TestImporter_Verify_DetectsDrift exercises the read-back path from Axon target data rather than only comparing in-memory source fixtures.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... -run 'TestImporter_Verify_DetectsDrift' passes.
4. cd cli && go test ./... passes, or any failure is documented as unrelated environment/repo pre-existing failure with this child’s focused test passing.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification that reads migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and detects field-level drift. Drift detection should be independently executable from clean round-trip fixture expansion, dry-run behavior, write-path apply mechanics, and CLI routing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer exposes MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If verifyImportedAxonCorpus or its comparison helpers are absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when stored Axon data differs from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so verification reads back the imported Axon target corpus, compares migrated source beads field-for-field, and returns an error that names the affected bead ID and the drifted field when target data is changed post-import. Keep implementation compatible with existing sample-based verification if a corpus-size threshold already exists; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or the full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Dry-run counting/no-mutation semantics; sibling child owns dry-run behavior.
- Clean round-trip fixture breadth for attachment/extras preservation; sibling child owns that proof.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

GOVERNING CONTEXT
Spec: TD-027. Decomposition parent: ddx-53df5e2f. Upstream parent/dependency context: ddx-3d96c6f9.

PROBLEM
Attempt 20260713T145533-c006900a for ddx-8a78ee90 ran for 32m43s with a populated Codex route, repeatedly executing a known-doomed 600-second package suite. The documented 30-minute running-phase watchdog did not fire because route activity kept the attempt classified as healthy.

Keep the default at 30 minutes for queue-attempt lease budgeting. NON-SCOPE
Do not shorten the generic ddx run three-hour provider cap. Do not change queue ordering, provider routing, the phase-empty watchdog, or long-running bead acceptance commands. Do not rely on process ancestry alone. Do not implement sibling lease-continuation, manual/server parity, or descendant-reaping behavior except where needed to wire the wall-clock expiry path.

Without a dedicated consumer bead, publishing v0.15 would leave this forbidden boundary crossing in DDx indefinitely.

- cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:42-169 plus orphan_harness_reaper_linux.go:22-113 discovers and kills orphan harness processes.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1249-1258 and execute_bead_loop.go:1616-1618 retain attempt-end and liveness integration.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process.go:61-195 and cli/internal/server/workers_reap_unix.go:33-213 mix Fizeau-owned descendants into otherwise DDx-owned attempt/worker cleanup.
- Fizeau containment epic fizeau-c795e7d9 is closed, but release bead fizeau-b9a2037c must publish and prove cancellation/caller-death cleanup before DDx removes the fallback.

PROPOSED FIX
After pinning the compatible Fizeau release, add consumer conformance proving Execute cancellation and caller death terminate every wrapped harness/provider process tree. Delete the PATH shim, hidden provider-launch command/platform implementation, concrete provider binary list, provider-child/orphan-harness census and reapers, route-aware child liveness, attempt-end provider reap, and provider-descendant branches in generic cleanup. DDx retains only cancellation of the context supplied to Fizeau Execute and may supervise/reap DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, and container processes. No concrete returned route fact may authorize a signal.

NON-SCOPE

description:
PROBLEM
Operators cannot tell whether reusable attempt workspaces are being used because execute-bead preparation and cleanup do not emit hit, miss, or cold-start observability events for reusable workspace slots.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces without emitting reuse-specific observability events.
- No hit/miss counters exist in the attempt path, leaving no signal for slot reuse behavior.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, the child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Emit reusable workspace hit, miss, and cold-start counts through the existing execution event/observability path from execute-bead orchestration. Scope events by project identity, worker-slot identity, resolved backend policy, and attempt identity for both reuse and cold-start attempts.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx needs MET-003 loss attribution to distinguish Fizeau lifecycle cause/stage from DDx-owned owner/stage evidence. Collapsing those fields during attempt-policy adaptation would make policy route-neutral but attribution ambiguous.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6569-6627 fills OutcomeReason from Detail/Error/Stderr when reports lack a typed reason, blending external cause details with DDx report evidence. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go:104-242 derives failure modes from mixed status, exit code, and error text. Phase 1 WB-1 requires typed Fizeau lifecycle signals plus DDx-owned stage evidence to be adapted exactly once: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:128-143.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the adapter input/output or report construction path so Fizeau cause/stage and DDx owner/stage evidence are stored as distinct fields. Ensure the policy decision can reference both sources without merging their meanings, and keep the separation visible in tests for MET-003 attribution.

description:
PROBLEM
Operator-attention filled with 31 "successful result commit was preserved for manual landing" items. Survey against HEAD (2026-08-02): 19 merge conflicts, 8 missing preserve refs, 4 clean merges. Missing/conflict preserves sat for days until bulk human resolve --action retry. Workers never reclaimed them because status=proposed parks them outside ready.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_dangling_success.go:389-408 rejects conflicting lands only when a worker reclaims an in_progress dangling-success bead and Land returns preserved.
- parkDanglingSuccessForOperator (line 269-278) parks to proposed with needs-human meta; proposed beads never re-enter recoverDanglingSuccess until operator human-resolves.
- When preserve refs are missing (ref not in local repo) or conflict with current HEAD, there is no periodic re-evaluation that auto-rejects the result_rev and reopens the bead.

PROPOSED FIX
On human resolve --action retry OR on a scheduled OA recheck, if suggested_action names a preserve ref that is missing or merge-tree conflicts with HEAD, append preserved-result-rejected and open the bead without requiring operator hand-merge. Keep clean merges eligible for auto-land (existing Land path). Add TestDanglingSuccess_RejectsMissingPreserveRefOnRetry and TestDanglingSuccess_RejectsConflictingPreserveRefOnRetry.

NON-SCOPE
Do not force-merge conflicting preserves. Do not delete preserve refs. Do not change close semantics for reachable result_revs.

description:
PROBLEM
The worker can keep holding claims while `server.unavailable` remains active, even after the server has become healthy again, which extends a transient probe failure into a queue-wide stall.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2182-2226` holds claims while `serverOutage.Active()` is true and only clears that state when the probe returns true. When combined with the over-strict resume probe, a healthy server can remain blocked until restart.

PROPOSED FIX
When the resume probe reports healthy, clear `server.unavailable` and continue draining ready beads immediately. Keep the claim hold only for genuine outages, not for transient smoke/provider failures once health is back.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove server outage handling for real TLS/transport failures. Do not demote thrashing beads. Do not disable pre-commit.

reliability P4/P10; FEAT-010 work loop stay-alive.

description:
PROBLEM
A ddx work worker can spend minutes synchronously measuring and deleting one accumulated scratch tree before it claims useful work. During the 2026-07-13 niflheim incident, one cleanup pass performed hundreds of megabytes of physical reads; the same path timed out at both 120 seconds in isolation and 600 seconds in the full package gate. This creates unbounded CPU/I/O latency and makes queue progress inversely proportional to stale cache size.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1687 runs the execution cleanup pass on the claim path. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:620-747 scans every matching scratch directory, calls measureTreeWithContext over an unbounded tree, and then calls os.RemoveAll, which walks the tree again and cannot observe context cancellation. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 includes the shared cache parent and legacy process temp directory by default. A large stale directory therefore monopolizes the single queue worker with no per-pass item, inode, byte, or wall-clock budget.

PROPOSED FIX
- Put a deterministic wall-clock/work budget around scratch discovery, measurement, and reclamation on worker passes.
- Make cancellation effective during both measurement and deletion; do not enter an uninterruptible whole-tree RemoveAll after the budget expires.
- Persist or rediscover unfinished candidates safely so later passes continue reclamation without restarting an O(tree) measurement from zero.
- Return a non-fatal structured deferred-cleanup observation when the budget is exhausted, then allow candidate selection to proceed.
- Preserve liveness, ownership, registered-worktree, and minimum-age checks before any mutation.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go only as needed for the bounded pass contract
- focused cleanup tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not delete live worktrees, reduce the six-hour minimum age, disable cleanup, or treat cleanup deferral as bead failure.

PARENT
None; root production reliability regression.

DEPS
Depends on ddx-e6abf4a6 so the hermetic test boundary lands before production cleanup stress tests run.

description:
PROBLEM
Commit `020853315` added `ListModelsWithProbeContainment`, which fixes the immediate leaked-probe symptom but identifies ownership by taking a process-wide provider baseline and reaping every provider descendant that appears afterward. A concurrent legitimate provider started under the same worker after the baseline can therefore be killed as if it belonged to this discovery call. Both scans use `context.Background()`, each termination can wait independently, and cleanup scan/termination errors are discarded, so the containment path can itself wedge or report false success.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go:28-35` attributes all post-baseline provider descendants to one `ListModels` call without a call-owned process/session identity.
- `cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go:38-64` runs both baseline and cleanup through `context.Background()` and drops cleanup errors.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children_unix.go:18-58` enumerates the host through `ps` and flattens descendants without PPID, process-group, session, or launch-owner metadata needed to prove call ownership.

PROPOSED FIX
Use an exact call-owned provider/session handle from the Fizeau cancellation work in `ddx-a751a7b1` when available and remove the process-wide baseline sweep. If a local fallback is still required, retain ancestry/session/launch ownership, serialize ambiguous lifecycle discovery, bound baseline and cleanup enumeration with explicit deadlines, fail closed by preserving ambiguous processes, and surface cleanup failures in the returned error and execution evidence. Cleanup must never wait on `context.Background()` or kill a provider solely because it appeared after a PID snapshot.

NON-SCOPE
Do not disable model discovery, extend the caller timeout, kill manual provider sessions, kill active implementation harnesses or their fixtures, weaken attempt-end cleanup, or change route selection.

PARENT
`ddx-f84ee9a7` (Niflheim provider-test CPU incident).

DEPS
Related to `ddx-a751a7b1` for the preferred upstream call-owned cancellation handle and `ddx-44e89575` for provider ancestry ownership; no hard dependency so the bounded fail-closed fallback can land independently.

description:
PROBLEM
Even after a typed attempt-policy adapter exists, execute-bead report construction can still backfill OutcomeReason from untyped detail, error, and stderr fields. That keeps legacy text-derived policy behavior alive in the execution loop.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6569-6627 fills OutcomeReason from Detail/Error/Stderr when the report lacks a typed reason. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go:104-242 derives failure modes from status, exit code, and error text. Phase 1 WB-1 requires completed, retryable, unavailable-now, cancelled, and permanent Fizeau lifecycle outcomes to flow through one DDx adapter exactly once: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:128-143.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire execute-bead report construction and status handling to call the typed DDx attempt-policy adapter for completed, retryable, unavailable-now, cancelled, and permanent failure cases. Store Fizeau cause/stage separately from DDx owner/stage evidence for MET-003 loss attribution. Preserve route identity only as audit evidence. Keep legacy text tables only where still needed for compatibility outside the new adapter path.

NON-SCOPE
Do not select a harness, provider, model, or route. Do not parse Fizeau stderr. Do not make Fizeau own bead state, review policy, landing, or closure. Do not delete all legacy text tables in this bead except where needed to route the new adapter. Fizeau internal routing, provider selection, provider retry, and provider-specific protocols remain non-scope. Review content, direct provider integration in DDx, timeboxed DDx bypasses, direct-provider fallback, and Fizeau demotion/replacement are non-scope. Do not expand the set of DDx decisions beyond current-attempt repair, new-attempt retry, minimum-strength escalation request, park, land, and close.

PARENT
Preserve parent reference ddx-b8cacbeb. Source decomposition parent field: ddx-66a8883f.

DEPS
Depends on the child bead that pins the compatible Fizeau typed lifecycle contract and on the child beads that add the typed adapter and route-neutral provider-identity tests. Preserve upstream dependency IDs fizeau#fizeau-8440f9ec and fizeau#fizeau-9d2c83e8. Preserve governing WB-1 references to fizeau#fizeau-6f9ffa71, fizeau#fizeau-c795e7d9, and fizeau#fizeau-022cbb9a.

description:
PROBLEM
Reusable attempt workspaces need a post-reset integrity gate. If reset/scrub fails to prove the workspace is clean, DDx must quarantine the slot instead of returning unsafe state to the reusable pool. Healthy slots should still be returned to the pool after successful cleanup.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- There is no reset/scrub integrity failure path in `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go`, so unsafe reusable state would otherwise be indistinguishable from healthy reusable state.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) currently remove workspaces rather than validating reusable slot health before reuse.

PROPOSED FIX
Add post-reset/scrub integrity validation for reusable slots in both linked-worktree and local-clone cleanup paths. A failed integrity check must quarantine the slot, prevent future reuse, and emit operator-visible diagnostics containing slot, backend, project, and reason. A successful cleanup and integrity check must return only healthy slots to the pool for future sequential reuse.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this child concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement repository identity mismatch, cleanup-failure quarantine, or live-process quarantine behavior except as minimal fixtures needed for integrity/healthy-return coverage.

description:
PROBLEM
The normal internal/agent unit-test gate reads and deletes host-global DDx scratch trees. On 2026-07-13, TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim drove about 431 MB of physical reads, timed out after 120 seconds in isolation, and caused the required 600-second package gate to time out. This makes test duration depend on accumulated host cache state and adds substantial I/O/CPU pressure while ddx work is trying to drain the queue.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go:269-288 creates a production NewExecutionCleanupManager for t.TempDir but does not override TempRoot or ScratchRoots. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 therefore derives the shared cache parent and legacy process temp directory. Cleanup reaches cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:620-747, where it recursively measures and removes every old matching scratch directory. The timeout stack was in measureTreeWithContext from cleanupScratchRoots, not in the predispatch fixture under test.

PROPOSED FIX
- Give every execution-cleanup unit fixture an explicit hermetic TempRoot and ScratchRoots beneath its own t.TempDir before calling Cleanup.
- Add a shared test helper if needed so future fixtures cannot silently fall back to ~/.cache/ddx or the process temp root.
- Add a sentinel/tripwire proving the loop-cleanup test cannot enumerate, measure, or remove a scratch root outside its fixture root.
- Audit adjacent NewExecutionCleanupManager test call sites reached by ./internal/agent and apply the same boundary where they invoke Cleanup.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go and nearest cleanup test helpers as required

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production cleanup, change retention policy, or skip cleanup assertions. Production cleanup latency is tracked separately.

PARENT
None; root gate-reliability regression.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a mapping row that points to a nonexistent inspectable runtime artifact or uses a command that is not on the executable verification allowlist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifacts or arbitrary prose commands rather than current-revision executable evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The requested spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the parent analyzer work has not yet added runtime-artifact existence checks or command allowlist enforcement for Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires each mapping row to name an exact evidence target and allowlisted executable verification command, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, which requires rejecting mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
After the Verification mapping-parser child exposes row targets and commands, add checks for inspectable runtime artifacts and command allowlisting. A mapped artifact target must resolve to an existing repository path or generated fixture artifact that the analyzer can inspect without network access. A mapping row command must match the executable verification allowlist accepted by spechonesty. Emit a diagnostic for each nonexistent artifact target and each non-allowlisted command. Analyzer remains read-only and does not execute network-dependent checks.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go `Test*` symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks.

DEPS: parent ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

acceptance:
1. `TestWorktreeAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts` runs two sequential linked-worktree attempts, proves the second attempt receives the same healthy slot, and proves the workspace is reset to the second attempt's requested base revision.
2. `TestWorktreeAttemptBackendCleanupReturnsHealthySlot` proves successful linked-worktree cleanup returns the healthy slot to the allocator instead of unconditionally running `WorktreeRemove`.
3. `TestWorktreeAttemptBackendPreservesStaleRegistrationRecovery` proves `isStaleWorktreeRegistrationError` recovery at `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:157-173` still works after reusable-slot integration.
4. `TestWorktreeAttemptBackendKeepOnErrorPreservesExistingBehavior` proves `KeepOnError` still preserves the failed attempt workspace and does not return an unsafe slot.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'Test(WorktreeAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts|WorktreeAttemptBackendCleanupReturnsHealthySlot|WorktreeAttemptBackendPreservesStaleRegistrationRecovery|WorktreeAttemptBackendKeepOnErrorPreservesExistingBehavior)' -count=1` passes.
6. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/...` passes.
7. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes on the final staged tree.
description:
PROBLEM
`WorktreeAttemptBackend` creates and removes an attempt-specific linked worktree for every bead attempt, so sequential attempts cannot reuse a healthy workspace even when a bounded reusable slot pool is available.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare`) creates a fresh linked worktree at an attempt-specific path via `gitOps.WorktreeAdd`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:157-173` handles stale worktree registration recovery, but only in the fresh-create path.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) unconditionally runs `WorktreeRemove`, discarding any healthy workspace.

PROPOSED FIX
Build on the sibling bead `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface` and do not start this child until that allocator/config surface lands. Teach `WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare` to request a project-local worker slot, verify health and repository identity, reset the linked worktree to the requested base revision, and reuse it across sequential attempts. Teach successful cleanup to return the healthy worktree slot to the pool instead of unconditionally removing it. Preserve existing stale-worktree-registration recovery and `KeepOnError` behavior.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this child concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement local-clone reuse in this child except through shared helpers needed by linked-worktree reuse.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-96fae203 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
During autonomous drain on eitri (2026-08-04/05), ddx work --watch workers repeatedly entered phase=server.unavailable with message "server unreachable: holding queue until /api/health returns" while curl https://127.0.0.1:7743/api/health returned {"status":"ok"}. Steward had to kill/restart workers 3+ times in one babysit window after land/pre-commit attempts (especially RC8 go-test -race ./cmd). One bead-scoped failure must not park the entire worker indefinitely when the coordination server is healthy (P4 blast radius, P10 self-unstick).

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
1. Resume probe couples liveness to agent smoke, not health:
   cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:353-389 serverHealthProbe GETs /api/health then requires agent.RunWithConfigViaService(... Prompt: "server health smoke test") ExitCode==0. If health is OK but smoke fails (routing, provider, transient LLM error), Healthy returns false forever.
2. Watch loop holds claims while serverOutage.Active() (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2182-2226) and only clears on probe true.
3. Outage activation can fire from report text / no-viable-provider thresholds (cli/internal/agent/server_outage.go:91-122, isServerTransportFailureText:148-161) after non-transport land failures; recovery then depends on the over-strict smoke probe.

Observed: after ddx-dee23a4d / ddx-49e799f9 task_succeeded + long pre-commit, workers stuck server.unavailable despite /api/health ok until process restart.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Split probes: liveness for resume = /api/health HTTP 200 only (or health + optional cheap non-LLM smoke). Do not require a Fizeau Execute success to clear server.unavailable.
2. Optionally keep a separate degraded-routing signal that does not claim "server unreachable" or hold the queue on health-ok hosts.
3. On Activate, log the report detail that triggered outage (bead_id, failure snippet) so false positives are diagnosable.
4. Tests: TestServerHealthProbeResumesOnHealthOKWithoutAgentSmoke; TestServerOutageDoesNotActivateOnPreCommitPackageFailureText (if currently matched).

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove server outage handling for real TLS/transport failures. Do not demote thrashing beads. Do not disable pre-commit.

PARENT
ddx-b79130f2

GOVERNING
reliability P4/P10; FEAT-010 work loop stay-alive.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestServerHealthProbeResumesOnHealthOKWithoutAgentSmoke: with /api/health 200 and agent smoke failing/unavailable, watch loop clears server.unavailable and claims next ready bead.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

1. TestAgentGitConfigEnvSanitizesRepositorySelection proves the shared fixture git helper clears inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` before any fixture `git config` write, while still binding commands to the intended temporary repository.
2. TestAgentGitConfigHelperUsesPrivateConfig proves `core.bare`, `core.worktree`, `user.name`, and `user.email` writes through the fixture helper land only in the temporary fixture repository/config scope and not in the invoking checkout's common config.
3. TestAgentGitConfigHelperFailsClosedWhenPrivateScopeUnavailable proves setup returns a deterministic error before mutation when the helper cannot establish a fixture-private config scope.
4. `cd cli && CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./internal/agent/... -run "Test(AgentGitConfigEnvSanitizesRepositorySelection|AgentGitConfigHelperUsesPrivateConfig|AgentGitConfigHelperFailsClosedWhenPrivateScopeUnavailable)" -count=20` passes.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s` passes.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Agent tests and fixture helpers that call `git config` can select the invoking checkout's shared common gitdir instead of a temporary fixture repository. When a fixture writes values such as `core.bare=true`, `core.worktree`, `user.name`, or `user.email`, the full agent test suite can corrupt the repository configuration used by the primary checkout and linked worktrees.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:20-55 enables worktree config and seeds per-worktree config for execute-bead isolation, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:169-229 wraps commands executed through the agent harness. Fixture setup paths such as runGitInteg/newScriptHarnessRepo are outside that production wrapper and can inherit `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, or common-config selection from the caller, so `git config` can target the shared repository config.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce or harden a shared helper used by agent test fixtures and subprocess setup so every git invocation that may read or write repository configuration is explicitly bound to the temporary fixture repository or a fixture-private config scope. The helper must clear inherited repository-selection environment (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and related config selectors as applicable) unless it deliberately sets fixture-local values. Production execute-bead callers must remain wired through the same isolation helper surface instead of growing an ad hoc test-only workaround.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the existing core.bare/core.worktree repair behavior, remove execute-bead config isolation, alter user project Git configuration, or change DDx/Fizeau routing. This child owns helper-level test and execution-isolation correctness only; stale index-lock recovery is ddx-3f156500 and main-git lock safety is ddx-1c8d9319. Parent bead: ddx-8b22914e. Deps: none; independent defect discovered while validating ddx-3f156500.

description:
PROBLEM
A missing runtime artifact diagnostic is not actionable unless it identifies the mapping row context that caused it. The parent behavior requires the diagnostic to identify the offending artifact path, requirement id, and source document so the document owner can fix the exact Verification row.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Populate the missing-artifact diagnostic emitted by spechonesty runtime-artifact validation with the artifact path exactly as written in the mapping row, the requirement id from that row, and the source document path that contains the row. Reuse the mapping-parser row model for source metadata and do not infer missing context from prose. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add new categories of diagnostics beyond missing inspectable runtime artifact mappings. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. description:
PROBLEM
On Niflheim, the managed DDx worker spawned `codex --no-alt-screen` PID 1760621 during pre-claim route/model discovery. The readiness route resolved and its intake provider exited, but the PTY probe remained a direct worker child for more than 123 seconds, initially consuming about 11% CPU, until the operator killed only its process group. A two-second DDx discovery deadline therefore returns control without stopping the work it started, allowing every queue poll to accumulate provider CPU.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:519-533` gives `svc.ListModels(modelCtx, modelFilter)` a two-second context.
- Fizeau v0.14.50 `internal/serviceimpl/subprocess_discovery_cache.go:74-94` accepts a refresh context but discards it and calls context-free `DefaultModelSnapshot()`; its warm/cold paths at :106-149 can launch refresh in a background goroutine after the caller returns.
- Fizeau v0.14.50 `internal/harnesses/codex/model_discovery.go:20-48` runs `codex --no-alt-screen` through `ptyquota.Run(context.Background(), ...)`, severing both the DDx caller deadline and worker lifecycle cancellation.
- This regresses the containment intent of closed bead `ddx-403e9a23`, whose server-side workaround explicitly left upstream context propagation out of scope.

PROPOSED FIX
Upgrade to a Fizeau release that carries caller/lifecycle context through cached subprocess discovery into `ptyquota.Run`, or patch the dependency first and then update `cli/go.mod` and `cli/go.sum`. An asynchronous cache refresh must own a bounded context, and every success, error, timeout, and cancellation path must wait until the spawned PTY session/process group is gone. Add a DDx call-site regression around lifecycle model discovery. If an upstream release cannot land in the same pass, add a narrowly scoped DDx containment layer that tracks and reaps only discovery descendants created by this call; never scan for or kill unrelated user provider processes.

NON-SCOPE
Disabling model discovery, extending the two-second caller timeout, killing manual Codex sessions or provider processes that predate the call, changing route selection, or restarting the DDx server.

PARENT
None; root reliability/performance regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-092f0d34` (preclaim lifecycle containment) and regression of `ddx-403e9a23`; neither relation permits killing processes outside the current worker/call baseline.

4. TestValidationSupervisor_CancelReapsSessionChangingDescendants proves attempt cancellation and server shutdown remove the command plus setsid/reparented descendants, persist a non-success result, and emit operator_attention with attempt, bead, validation ID, fingerprint, and last activity.

description:
PROBLEM
A bead can require a validation timeout longer than the harness shell tool permits. In ddx-5653688f attempt 20260713T195457-44c4a97d, cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent was still making progress with one bounded test process when the Codex bash tool forcibly terminated it at 20m20.150s with exit 143. The model then tried the same command through background shell, nohup, and Python start_new_session wrappers to evade the tool ceiling. The first two died with their tool shells; the third survived by reparenting to the user systemd manager inside ddx-server.service, leaving DDx unable to attach an exit status or automatically associate that process with the attempt. A valid 30-minute acceptance gate therefore cannot complete through the normal path and provokes exactly the detached replay behavior DDx forbids.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2085-2094 expresses long-command safety only as prompt text. It says to stop after incomplete evidence but provides no DDx-owned way to run a command beyond a harness tool ceiling.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_long_running_fixture_test.go:102-145 explicitly calls prompt-only enforcement sufficient and tests only that phrases exist, not that a long gate can finish once or that detached recovery is contained.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:25-35 observes a tool call only until its result/deadline; it does not own a separately addressable validation subprocess that a later tool call can reattach to.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:10-39 contains only the harness process group. A command intentionally launched with start_new_session can leave harness ancestry even though it remains in the aggregate server cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX
Create one attempt-owned validation supervisor before the model harness starts and expose a small start/status/await client surface to the model. A long command must be registered by normalized command, cwd, environment/config, and tracked-worktree fingerprint; the supervisor launches it inside the attempt controller, persists stdout/stderr and the real exit status under the execution bundle, and continues when an individual harness tool call reaches its ceiling. Reissuing start for the same fingerprint must reattach to the existing run rather than launch a duplicate. Cancellation, attempt exit, or server death must reap the supervised command and session-changing descendants. The same supervisor/client contract must work for manual/offline and server-managed workers; managed descendants remain in ddx-server.service and die with the service. Replace prompt-only snapshot confidence with behavioral integration coverage.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not infer success from exit 143, missing exit evidence, a PID-only file, or a killed command.
- Do not permit arbitrary detached daemons outside an attempt controller.
- Do not weaken project-declared validation timeouts or skip long tests; ddx-85d27282 separately removes a chaos matrix from short mode.
- Do not duplicate semantic replay detection owned by parent ddx-7fb837a0 or the CPU envelope owned by ddx-7df6b12a.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent ddx-7fb837a0. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for attempt-controller containment and cleanup.
